rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest, L35 (chunk 3 "Leave it out of the plan..."): "A wrong call about which interviews count spreads into every page written after it." Interviews appear nowhere earlier in the file, but it is an indefinite example inside a self-explaining sentence, not a pronoun or demonstrative awaiting an antecedent, and the plan/agent/pages it needs are all named in-chunk. Harm (unresolvable referent) absent. Header "it" (L32) is generic and resolved by the body's first sentence. L25 "around it" = the stance named in the same bullet.

grep -nEi "(opening|earlier|previous|last|first) (lecture|module|exercise)|you (did|saw)" over body-numbered lines 1-50 of expanded view: 0 hits. Only in-file callback is L49-50 "the draft", which is chunk 4's own subject (L46).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L17 "The first exchange became part of context": resolves to L9/L11 in the same chunk. No "the X you did/saw/caught" phrasing anywhere in the four chunks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1 L13 guess cue ("Before you read on, take a guess. What will it suggest?") precedes the L15 reveal ("Claude suggests something Finnish"); L9 narrates only the first window's answer, which is the setup, not the reveal. Scene is verbed (L7-11), cue addresses the reader not the terminal. Guard note on source slide attests the shape (Antti 2026-10-06, curriculum/slides/same-question-two-answers.md L21). Muted read: nothing depends on a screen or trainer.

All four chunks carry a self-standing claim: chunk 1 L17 "The first exchange became part of context, and the context colored everything after."; chunk 2 L24-26; chunk 3 L35; chunk 4 L46. Shortest is chunk 3 at three short paragraphs, none a wait-state.

Closest: chunk 1 header "Same question, two answers" (L4), a label; literally true (identical second prompt L9/L11, different answers L9/L15). Chunk 2 header (L21) names Bring/Set/Ask, matching bolded leads L24-26 exactly. Chunk 3 header (L32) is stated by L35; chunk 4 header (L43) by L46-50.

Per chunk: no "Not X. Not Y. Z." (grep -c "Not .*\. Not " = 0); no anaphora triple (closest L37 "what it will read, what it will write, and where" is one list inside a sentence, third leg "where" adds content); no self-grading superlative; no number+retraction; no abstraction-noun stack (closest L25 "what one pass lets through" is concrete); verb triplet Bring/Set/Ask (L24-26) each survives "what does this concretely mean" with its own example. L48 "a claim about your product, not a verdict" is a single contrast, not the banned construction.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -niE "surface|firing|compendium|forcing function|beat|mood|connections" over body lines 1-50 of expanded view: 0 hits. Closest L24 "stance" and L25 "check" are ordinary product-team words.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only bold: L24-26 **Bring**, **Set**, **Ask**, one word each, named in the chunk header (L21) as the three handles; checklist-item-name case, inside the ≲5-word cap and the one-handle-per-item allowance. Chunks 1, 3, 4 carry no bold. Closest to violating: three bolds on one slide, which the header-named handle set licenses.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture is included as a standalone-paragraph lecture line in curriculum/trainings/agentic-product-teams-101/our-product-our-system.md L50, so it sits under a lecture wrapper; expanded view shows all four slide files inlined as ## chunks (L4, L21, L32, L43); node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file reports slides: 4. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture headings are claims: L21 "You steer with what you bring, what you set and what you ask", L32 "Leave it out of the plan and the agent decides", L43 "On your own product, you are the check". Closest: L4 "Same question, two answers", a demo-opener label, not a law or consolidation slide, so the claim requirement does not bind it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L39 "One correction to the plan can redirect every step after it." mirrors L35 "spreads into every page written after it" but supplies the payoff that justifies the L37 ask (a cheap fix at plan stage), which the slide does not otherwise state; not a koan restating the header. L28 "Each one needs someone who knows the product." adds the hand-off to chunk 4's argument. No doctrine restatement, no pedagogy commentary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: git log shows chunk 2 and chunk 3 headers retitled in b758b28b ("You steer the agent in three ways" -> L21; "Ask for the plan before the agent writes" -> L32). Cover-the-body test: L21 promises bring/set/ask, L24-26 deliver exactly those; L32 promises "left open, the agent decides", L35 opens with exactly that, then L37 gives the move. No bullet answers the old header only.
